incidentId.description: Positive integer uniquely identifying the ICM incident (e.g., 1234567) used to retrieve the similar incidents. Must not contain non-numeric characters or whitespace

tools.name: ICMPlugin_GetIncidentMitigationHints

incidentId.description: Positive integer uniquely identifying the ICM incident (e.g., 1234567) used to get mitigation hints, Must not contain non-numeric characters or whitespace

tools.name: ICMPlugin_GetIncidentContext
tools.description: Gets context for the specified incident. Use for bridge summary/recap, bridge details, incident history, outage details, and other context metadata.

incidentId.description: Positive integer uniquely identifying the ICM incident (e.g., 1234567) used to retrieve the context. Must not contain non-numeric characters or whitespace

tools.name: ICMPlugin_GetIncidentSummary
tools.description: Retrieves the AI-generated incident summary for a given incident. Use for overall incident summary requests only; do not use for incident links/URLs, bridge summaries/recaps, incident history, or outage context.

incidentId.description: Positive integer uniquely identifying the ICM incident (e.g., 1234567) used to retrieve the summary. Must not contain non-numeric characters or whitespace

tools.name: ICMDataPlugin_QueryIncidents
tools.description: Query IcM incidents based on the provided parameters. Use this to find active outages, triage incidents, or review recent incident history. Usage guidance:- To find incidents owned by a specific team, set teamName (e.g., 'Telemetry'). To find incidents under a specific tenant/service, set tenantNameList (e.g., ['Skype'], ['Skype Teams', 'Cosmic']). Combine teamName and tenantNameList to narrow results (e.g., teamName='Networking', tenantNameList=['Cosmic']).

startPeriod.description: The number defining the start of the time period, measured using units in periodTimeUnit (for example, startPeriod=90 with periodTimeUnit=Day means 90 days ago). Default value is 90.

endPeriod.description: The number defining the end of the time period, measured using units in periodTimeUnit (for example, endPeriod=0 with periodTimeUnit=Day means now). Default value is 0 (now).

periodTimeUnit.description: The unit of the time period specified by startPeriod and endPeriod. Default value is 'Day'.

showOutagesOnly.description: Whether to limit results to outages only. Default value is false (all incidents).

statusList.description: The statuses to include: ACTIVE, MITIGATED, RESOLVED, CORRELATING, HOLDING, NEW

teamName.description: The IcM team name.Do NOT provide a value unless the user explicitly states it. Leave null — the system resolves this automatically.

tenantNameList.description: The IcM tenant/service name(s). When the user mentions multiple tenants or services, include ALL of them in this single list and call the tool only once. Do NOT make separate calls per tenant.

keywordList.description: The list of keywords to filter incidents by. Prefix each keyword with INCLUDE: or EXCLUDE: to control filtering.INCLUDE: keywords match incidents containing that term (default if no prefix).EXCLUDE: keywords remove incidents containing that term.At most 10 keywords are used across INCLUDE and EXCLUDE entries; each keyword is capped at 128 characters after trimming and prefix removal.Example: ['INCLUDE:deployment', 'EXCLUDE:Ring Blocker']

tools.name: ICMDataPlugin_QueryRetrospectives
tools.description: Query IcM retrospectives (postmortems) based on the user-provided parameters. (e.g. Show me retrospectives for Telemetry team -> set teamName to 'Telemetry')

startDay.description: The number of days to look back to define the date range start.

endDay.description: The number of days to look back to define the date range end. Default value is 0 (today).

statusList.description: The statuses to include: AIDRAFT, INPROGRESS, READYFORREVIEW, COMPLETED, ABANDONED

teamName.description: The IcM team name. Do NOT provide a value unless the user explicitly states it. Leave null — the system resolves this automatically.

tenantNameList.description: The IcM tenant/service name(s). When the user mentions multiple tenants or services, include ALL of them in this single list and call the tool only once. Do NOT make separate calls per tenant.

keywordList.description:
The list of keywords to filter retrospectives by. Prefix each keyword with INCLUDE: or EXCLUDE: to control filtering.
INCLUDE: keywords match retrospectives containing that term (default if no prefix).
EXCLUDE: keywords remove retrospectives containing that term.
At most 10 keywords are used across INCLUDE and EXCLUDE entries; each keyword is capped at 128 characters after trimming and prefix removal.
Examples: ['INCLUDE:deployment', 'EXCLUDE:Ring Blocker']

tools.name: ICMDataPlugin_GetPagedIncidents
tools.description: Retrieve the incidents that paged/notified the on-call for a team in the given time period. This plugin should only be invoked to get the paged incidents for DRI/IM handoff scenarios.

startPeriod.description: The number defining the start of the time period. Default value is 12.

endPeriod.description: The number defining the end of the time period. Default value is 0 (now).

periodTimeUnit.description: The unit of the time period: day, hour. Default value is 'hour'.

teamId.description: The IcM team id (example: 28401). Optional, if none provided the user's team information will be used.

tools.name: ICMPlugin_GetsOnCallsByIncidentId
tools.description: Retrieves the contact information of engineers/managers who are on-call right now for a given incident id. On-call may also refer to DRI (Designated Responsible Individual) or IM (Incident Manager).

incidentId.description: Positive integer uniquely identifying the ICM incident (e.g., 1234567) used to retrieve the summary. Must not contain non-numeric characters or whitespace

tools.name: ICMPlugin_GetsOnCallsByDescription
tools.description: Retrieves the contact information of engineers/managers who are on-call right now based on the given team description. On-call may also refer to DRI (Designated Responsible Individual), IM (Incident Manager). This is used to provide operations support for incidents, DO NOT use to find privacy or security champs. If the user is asking for an IM/Incident Manager, append 'Incident Manager' to the team descriptor if not specified. Examples: 1. Who is on call for Client Release team? -> Client Release. 2. Who is IM for Teams today -> Teams Incident Manager. 3. Get DRI for SKYPETEAMS\livesite-tooling -> SKYPETEAMS\livesite-tooling 4. Who is Teams Incident Manager -> Teams Incident Manager

teamDescriptor.description: A user-provided reference to an IcM team. This can be a full or partial team name or public ID (e.g., 'Performance', 'TenantName\TeamName').

tools.name: repo_pull_request
tools.description: Read operations on Azure DevOps pull requests. Use 'action' to choose: 'get' [requires repositoryId, pullRequestId, project] — get a PR by ID; 'list' [requires repositoryId OR project] — list PRs with optional filters; 'list_by_commits' [requires project, repository, commits] — find PRs containing the given commits; 'get_changes' [requires repositoryId, pullRequestId] — get file changes and line-by-line diffs for a PR iteration.

action.description: The operation to perform. One of: 'get', 'list', 'list_by_commits', 'get_changes'.

orgName.description: The Azure DevOps organization name. Required

repositoryId.description: Required for 'get' and 'get_changes'; optional for 'list' (used as a filter scope). For 'list_by_commits' use the 'repository' parameter instead. The ID or name of the repository. When a name is used, the project parameter must also be provided.

repository.description: Required for 'list_by_commits'. The ID or name of the repository.

project.description: Required for 'get' and 'list_by_commits'. Optional for 'list' (scopes the search). Required for 'get_changes' and other actions when repositoryId is a repository name (not a GUID). Project ID or project name.

pullRequestId.description: Required for 'get' and 'get_changes'. The ID of the pull request to retrieve.

includeWorkItemRefs.description: For 'get': Whether to reference work items associated with the pull request.

includeLabels.description: For 'get': Whether to include a summary of labels in the response.

top.description: For 'list': The maximum number of pull requests to return. For 'get_changes': The maximum number of file changes to return (default 100).

skip.description: For 'list': The number of pull requests to skip. For 'get_changes': The number of file changes to skip for pagination.

status.description: For 'list': Filter pull requests by status. Allowed values: 'Abandoned', 'Active', 'All', 'Completed', 'NotSet'.

sourceRefName.description: For 'list': Filter pull requests from this source branch (e.g., 'refs/heads/feature-branch').

targetRefName.description: For 'list': Filter pull requests into this target branch (e.g., 'refs/heads/main').

createdByMe.description: For 'list': Filter pull requests created by the current user. Ignored if createdByUser is provided.

iAmReviewer.description: For 'list': Filter pull requests where the current user is a reviewer. Ignored if userIsReviewer is provided.

userIsReviewer.description: For 'list': Filter pull requests where a specific user is a reviewer (provide email address). Takes precedence over iAmReviewer.

commits.description: For 'list_by_commits': Array of commit IDs to query for.

iterationId.description: For 'get_changes': The iteration ID to get changes for. If not specified, gets changes for the latest iteration.

compareTo.description: For 'get_changes': Iteration ID to compare against. If specified, returns changes between the two iterations.

includeDiffs.description: For 'get_changes': Whether to include actual line-by-line diff content. Default is true. Set to false to get only file metadata.

includeLineContent.description: For 'get_changes': Whether to include actual line content from the changed files. Default is true. When true, fetches file content and includes the code lines that were added/removed/modified.

pipelineVersion.description: For 'run_pipeline': Version of the pipeline to run. If not provided, the latest version will be used.

stagesToSkip.description: For 'run_pipeline': A list of stages to skip.

templateParameters.description: For 'run_pipeline': Custom build parameters as key-value pairs.

yamlOverride.description: For 'run_pipeline': YAML override. Only valid when previewRun=true.

name.description: For 'create_pipeline': Name of the new pipeline.

yamlPath.description: For 'create_pipeline': Path to a YAML file that already exists on the default branch of the target repo - verify with repo_file action=get_content before calling.

repositoryType.description: For 'create_pipeline': Required. The type of repository where the pipeline's YAML file is located.

repositoryName.description: For 'create_pipeline': For GitHub: 'owner/repo' (e.g., 'octocat/Hello-World'). For Azure Repos: the repo display name.

folder.description: For 'create_pipeline': Folder path for the new pipeline. Defaults to '\\' if not specified.

stageName.description: For 'update_build_stage': Exact stage name from the build's timeline.

status.description: For 'update_build_stage': New status for the stage (Cancel, Retry, Run).

forceRetryAllJobs.description: For 'update_build_stage': Whether to force retry all jobs in the stage.

op.description: The operation to perform on the field.

id.description: The ID of the work item to update.

path.description: The path of the field to update, e.g., '/fields/System.Title'.

value.description: The new value for the field. Accepts strings, numbers, booleans, or null (e.g. 3 for Priority, "Active" for State). This is required for 'Add' and 'Replace' operations, and should be omitted for 'Remove' operations.

format.description: The format of the field value. tools.name: testplan_test_run_write
tools.description: Write operations on Azure DevOps test runs and test points. Use 'action' to choose: 'create_run' (create a new test run for manual test execution; requires 'name', 'planId', 'pointIds'), 'update_results' (record outcomes, comments, and step-level results for test cases in a run; requires 'runId', 'results' JSON array), 'complete_run' (mark a test run as Completed or Aborted; requires 'runId'), 'update_test_point_outcome' (quick-mark test point outcomes without creating a run; requires 'planId', 'suiteId', 'testPointIds'; use 'outcome' to set Passed/Failed/etc. or set 'resetToActive' to true to clear the outcome). Typical workflow: create_run → update_results → complete_run. For 'complete_run': the API automatically determines the final state — if all test results have outcomes set, the run is marked 'Completed'; if any results lack outcomes, the run is marked 'Aborted'. For 'update_results', the 'results' JSON array elements have: 'id' (required, the test result ID — typically 100000 for single-result runs), 'outcome' (required — Passed, Failed, Blocked, NotExecuted, etc.), 'comment' (optional — shown in Analysis section), 'state' (optional — Pending, Queued, InProgress, Paused, Completed; defaults to Completed), 'failureType' (optional: None, Known Issue, New Issue, Regression). Step-level results support two modes (use one, not both): 1) 'stepResults' (simplified JSON array — auto-generates actionPath; each object has 'step' (1-based), 'outcome', 'errorMessage' (optional, shown as Comment in UI), 'iterationId' (optional, defaults to 1)). 2) 'iterationDetails' (full control for parameterized tests; each object has 'id' (iteration number starting at 1), 'outcome' (optional), 'actionResults' (JSON array with 'actionPath' (hex e.g. '00000002'), 'stepIdentifier', 'outcome', 'errorMessage' (optional), 'iterationId' (required, must match parent))). Tests containing shared steps are not supported.

tools.name: download_attachment
tools.title: Download Attachment
tools.description: Download a Viva Engage file attachment and return the bytes inline as base64. Pass the attachmentId returned by upload_attachment, or one of the IDs from a message's attachments connection (types: File, ImageFile, VideoFile). Fetches the bytes directly from Viva Engage with the same bearer token used for GraphQL — no separate SharePoint token is needed; Engage proxies SharePoint-backed files server-side. Returns the base64-encoded content along with filename (from Content-Disposition), MIME type, and size. Default size cap is 1 MiB per call (hard ceiling 4 MiB) — small enough to fit any MCP transport and LLM context after base64 expansion. Larger attachments are rejected as soon as the server advertises Content-Length. For attachments larger than the cap, pass startByte / endByte to fetch the file in chunks: the response includes a contentRange object with the chunk position and total file size so callers can drive multi-chunk downloads without separately tracking offsets. Callers that need the file on disk should decode the base64 themselves. SharePoint link attachments (SharePointFileLink, SharePointVideoLink, SharePointWebLink) and web links (WebLink, WebImage, WebVideo) are NOT supported — they have no uploaded file behind them; follow the link URL directly. Rate limit: each call counts as 1 request.

attachmentId.description: The ID of the attachment to download (File / ImageFile / VideoFile). Pass the attachmentId returned by upload_attachment, or one of the IDs from a message's attachments connection.

maxSizeInBytes.description: Maximum allowed attachment size in bytes. Defaults to 1 MiB (1048576); values above the 4 MiB (4194304) hard ceiling are rejected with a validation error — use startByte / endByte to page through larger attachments. When a byte range is requested this caps the size of the returned chunk, not the whole file. Downloads larger than this are rejected before any bytes are fetched.

startByte.description: Optional inclusive zero-based start of a byte range to fetch. Use together with endByte (or alone, to read from this offset to end-of-file) to download large attachments in chunks. The response's contentRange object reports the chunk's actual byte range and the total file size.

endByte.description: Optional inclusive zero-based end of a byte range to fetch. Use together with startByte (or alone, to read the first N+1 bytes) to limit the chunk size. Must be >= startByte when both are set.

tools.title: Get Community Posts
tools.description: Browse the feed of ONE specific community — by default the latest threads by recent activity (sortBy UPDATED_AT); set sortBy CREATED_AT for thread-creation/posting order. Use this only when the user wants to see what's happening in a community as a whole with no subject filter: "show me the latest posts in Engineering", "what's been happening in HR", "browse the Sales feed", "catch me up on All Company". This tool CANNOT filter by topic, keyword, or subject — if the user mentions what the posts are ABOUT ("posts about reorg", "anything on parental leave", "discussions on Q3 planning"), use `search` instead (it accepts a community filter via `contextCommunityId`). Returns threads with replies and Q&A posts (Viva Engage questions, not Teams Q&A/TQnA) — this is also where a community's open or unanswered questions live (QUESTION-type threads without an accepted answer). To narrow to a time window, pass ONE of afterDate or beforeDate: by default the window applies to THREAD-CREATION time (when a date is given with no explicit sortBy, the server sorts by CREATED_AT); to bound LAST-ACTIVITY time instead, also set `sortBy: UPDATED_AT`. To page through history, pass pageInfo.startCursor as `before` on the next call to walk backward. Each message includes a `type` field (MessageType enum: NORMAL, QUESTION, ARTICLE, POLL, PRAISE) — use it to determine the kind of message instead of inspecting boolean fields.

communityId.description: The ID of the community (the `id` field returned by feed, search, or get_communities tools).

count.description: Maximum number of threads to return per page (default: 10).

before.description: Cursor pointing to threads OLDER than this position. Use this to walk backward through history — pass pageInfo.startCursor from the previous response to fetch the next older page. Primary cursor for time-bounded queries like "threads from the past month".

after.description: Cursor pointing to threads NEWER than this position. Pass pageInfo.endCursor from a previous response to fetch threads created/updated since that point. Useful for "what's new since I last looked" workflows.

afterDate.description: Only return threads after the given time; ignored if the `after` cursor is also supplied. The bound applies to the axis `sortBy` selects — by default CREATED_AT (thread-creation time), or last-activity under `sortBy: UPDATED_AT`. Pass only ONE of afterDate/beforeDate; dates before 2019-01-31 are clamped to that floor.

beforeDate.description: Only return threads before the given time (exclusive); ignored if the `before` cursor is also supplied. Same axis rules as afterDate. A future value is treated as now (clamped by backend). Pass only ONE of afterDate/beforeDate.

sortBy.description: Sort order. Defaults to UPDATED_AT (last-activity); when afterDate/beforeDate is set with no explicit sort, defaults to CREATED_AT so the window applies to thread-creation time. RECOMMENDED cannot be combined with a date window.

feedType.description: Feed type filter (default: ALL). Options: ALL, QUESTIONS, QUESTIONS_WITH_NO_REPLIES, UNANSWERED_QUESTIONS (no best reply marked), RECOMMENDED, UNSEEN

previewLength.description: Maximum length of body preview text (default: 250)

previewTextOnly.description: When true (default), return only a short plain-text preview of each message body. Set false to include the full body via `content`, rendered in `bodyFormat`. Default true keeps feed scans lightweight.

bodyFormat.description: Format for the full message body when previewTextOnly is false: `Html` (default), `Markdown` (Engage-dialect Markdown), `PlainText`, or `ContentState` (raw Draft.js JSON). `content` may be null if that format is unavailable for a message.

Each message includes a `type` field (MessageType enum: NORMAL, QUESTION, ARTICLE, POLL, PRAISE) for determining the kind of message. Use for deep-dive on a specific thread, supporting metrics on a recent post, or grounding a follow-up agent action. Pass atMessageId to deep-link a specific reply and return its surrounding context instead of the most recent replies.

tools.name: get_custom_analytics_catalog

Requires the target thread's `threadId`: when the user identifies the thread by title or description (e.g. "make sure everyone in IT Help Desk sees the onboarding thread") rather than supplying an ID, first resolve the community with `get_communities` and locate the thread with `get_community_posts` to obtain its `threadId` before pinning.

tools.name: query_custom_analytics
tools.title: Query Custom Analytics
tools.description: Use this tool for catalog-driven aggregate analytics across communities, users, leaders, campaigns, audiences, or multiple conversations after calling get_custom_analytics_catalog. This includes time-bounded engagement, reach, views, reactions, replies, shares, bookmarks, and participants. Do not use feed-level counters as a substitute when these Custom Analytics tools are available. For content retrieval use get_conversation_by_id or get_user_posts; for dedicated single-post analytics use get_post_report when available. Queries caller-authorized custom analytics as a typed tabular result. Use the catalog to discover valid entity, dimension, and metric keys. The service derives the network from the signed-in user, enforces role-based scope, and only accepts allowlisted query vocabulary; this tool does not accept network IDs, SQL, or KQL.

tools.name: search
tools.title: Search
tools.description: Find content (read-only) by topic or keyword anywhere in Viva Engage — across all communities, or scoped to one. Use this whenever the user is looking FOR a subject: "posts about X", "discussions about X", "what people are saying about X", "find the thread where Y", "any conversations on Z", "has anyone mentioned W" — even when they name a specific community to look in (pass the community via `communityIds` or restrict thread results via `contextCommunityId`). Returns matched communities, people, threads, files, and topics. Each thread message includes a `type` field (MessageType enum: NORMAL, QUESTION, ARTICLE, POLL, PRAISE) for determining the kind of message. Every community position (root community results, thread scopes, broadcast/Teams-meeting host communities) carries `privacy` (Public, Private, or Moderated) and `sensitivityLabel` (compliance label, nullable) so callers can apply DLP / cross-network-quoting policy in a single round-trip. NOT a write or action tool — use this only for FINDING content, not for acting on a thread the user already knows about (mute, pin, feature, reply, edit, etc. each have their own tool). NOT for browsing a community feed chronologically with no topic filter — for that, use `get_community_posts`.

tools.name: upload_attachment
tools.description: Prepare an attachment for use with create_conversation or reply_in_thread. Supports two modes — provide exactly one of fileContentBase64 or url: (1) File upload: provide fileContentBase64 (the file's raw bytes, base64-encoded) together with filename to upload a file (images, documents, videos) via the internal 3-step flow (create session → upload binary → complete session). The bytes are sent inline because the server has no access to the caller's filesystem — a local path would not resolve on the server. The decoded file must be 4 MiB or smaller. Supported targets: community, storyline. (2) URL link preview: provide url to resolve a URL into an attachable link ID via the resolveWebLink mutation. This is required by the GraphQL schema — raw URLs cannot be attached directly. The mutation crawls the URL to extract OG metadata (title, description, preview image) and classifies the link type (WebLink, WebImage, WebVideo). Both modes return a unified attachmentId — pass it via attachmentIds to create_conversation or reply_in_thread. File and link IDs can be mixed in the same attachmentIds array. Rate limit: each call counts as 1 request (internal GraphQL and REST calls are not rate-limited separately), e.g. at the default 20 RPM you can prepare up to 20 attachments per minute.

fileContentBase64.description: The file's raw bytes, base64-encoded, to upload (decoded size must be 4 MiB or smaller). Provide this (with filename) OR url, not both.

url.description: URL to resolve into a rich link preview. Provide this OR fileContentBase64, not both.

filename.description: Display filename for the upload, including its extension (e.g. report.pdf). Required when fileContentBase64 is provided.

target.description: Upload target for file uploads. Ignored when url is provided.

communityId.description: The ID of the community (required for the community file upload target).

userId.description: The ID of the user (required for the storyline file upload target).

contextId.description: Context ID (Thread, User, or Community) for URL link resolution. Optional, ignored for file uploads.
